argument_summary: The admissible record does not support an unconditional claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy for the exposed Spanish-language billing support segment. It does support a narrower certification posture: aggregate launch readiness passed, monitored rollout and rollback are valid deployment controls, and public guidance recognizes monitoring plus disclosure of known limitations. On that record, the defensible position is conditional certification tied to explicit disclosure of the Spanish-language billing support limitation for the named launch use case and monitored rollout, rather than escalation based on an overbroad reading that certification was asserted without caveat.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The narrower caveated path preserves launch progress better than escalation while keeping the certification theory aligned to the admissible record.
claims_about_policy: Policy is not satisfied by 5% rollout, rollback, or monitoring alone when the affected segment remains exposed. The policy text allows rollout and post-launch monitoring to mitigate a material weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance. Neither is shown here. But the release policy separately requires disclosure of material limitations unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. That means the compliant path still available on the present record is caveated certification conditioned on disclosure of the known limitation, not unconditional certification and not reliance on the incomplete draft risk acceptance.
concessions: The Spanish-language billing support segment is below target and remains exposed in the initial random-account rollout.
The draft risk acceptance is incomplete, unapproved, and does not address the exposed Spanish-language billing support segment.
There is no admissible evidence here that disclosure has already been completed; the supportable position is certification only if treated as explicitly conditional on that disclosure.
The evidence does not support the broader claim that rollout controls alone cure the weakness.
